title: SLO integration prototype charter and stakeholder map
content:
Purpose and scope

This is a short, tactical charter for a 6-week cross-functional prototype to validate a lightweight SLO integration path for newly onboarded model-serving endpoints. It is intended to be run as an "ops field lab": a focused experiment that surfaces tooling gaps, handoff friction, and realistic measurement noise before we scale SLO requirements across product teams.

Goals (what success looks like)
- End-to-end pipeline from metric collection -> SLI computation -> SLO dashboarding -> automated alerting for one pilot service (model-serving v2).
- Verify feasibility of attributing latency/availability errors to routing, batching, and model-fallback policies with >= 90% accuracy for post-incident analysis.
- Produce a short remediation playbook and a small set of SLO templates (latency p95, availability 99.9%, tail-error budget) that a product team can adopt within 2 days.
- Quantify blind spots: metrics that are missing or high-cost to collect, and estimate implementation effort for the top-3 gaps.

Scope (in-scope / out-of-scope)
In-scope:
- Pilot on the "assistant-text-v2" serving route (dedicated capacity cluster), using prod-like load generator.
- Implement stream & batch SLI instrumentation (end-to-end latency, errors, fallback rate, model-version success rate).
- Build a Grafana dashboard and a Canary alert policy that triggers a Slack ops-bridge and a PagerDuty page if error budget burn rate exceeds threshold.
- Collate a short "adoption checklist" for product teams.

Out-of-scope:
- Global rollout or policy enforcement across all services.
- Deep integration with billing or cost-optimization systems.
- Long-term storage/retention changes — this prototype will use short retention (7d) only.

Team and stakeholders (who to loop in)
- Prototype lead (owner): Ava Chen (eng-sre) — overall coordination, experiments, and final write-up.
- Engineering: Marcus Ibrahim (serving-runtime) — instrumentation and SDK hooks.
- Product: Priya Natarajan (product-hosted-api) — product acceptance criteria and adoption checklist.
- Observability: Liam O'Rourke (observability) — dashboard + alert pipelines.
- Solutions/Onboarding: Sofia Martinez (solutions-engineering) — pilot adoption and developer-facing docs.
- Optional advisors: Performance researchers, Security reviewer for telemetry sampling.

High-level timeline (6 weeks)
Week 0 (planning, alignment)
- Kickoff workshop (2 hours) to agree goals, success metrics, and accept criteria. Tag: SRE-789 start.
- Confirm access and dataset for load generator.

Week 1-2 (instrumentation & baseline)
- Add SLI instrumentation to route (micro-tracing to capture prefix/KV cache hits, fallback events).
- Collect baseline for two days at prod-like qps.

Week 3 (dashboard + alerts)
- Implement Grafana dashboards and alert policies.
- Run a series of controlled degradation experiments (increase latencies, throttle capacity) and verify alerts fire appropriately.

Week 4-5 (attribution & handoff)
- Add tracing metadata to pinpoint whether incidents originate from hardware, model-layer, routing, or user workload.
- Run mixed-failure tests (simulate fallback and region failover).
- Draft handoff checklist and runbook.

Week 6 (retro & proposal)
- Compile results, cost estimates, and a proposed rollout plan for 3 more services.
- Share demo and decision brief with eng leadership and product.

Key experiments and acceptance criteria
1) End-to-end alerting: Inject 10% artificial latency for 30 minutes. Acceptance: alert fires within 5 minutes and indicates the correct symptom (latency at model-serving layer).
2) Attribution accuracy: For a set of 12 controlled incidents, automated event attribution matches manual postmortem labeling >= 90%.
3) Low-friction adoption: New product engineer can apply the SLO template and have working dashboard & alerts within two business days. Document time-to-adopt during prototype.

Observability & instrumentation notes
- Use existing SDK instrumentation in serving runtime; add lightweight tags for "batch_size", "route_variant", "kv_hit". Avoid heavy per-request sampling — leverage aggregated histogram exports for tails.
- Store SLIs in the observability workspace with 7d retention (short-term) and label by cluster/region/model-version.
- Traces: sample at 1% for normal traffic, bump to 10% during active experiments.

Communication and decision channels
- Daily 15-minute standup (Mon-Fri) in #sre-ops-lab Slack channel for the 6-week window.
- Decision checkpoint at end of week 3: green/yellow/red to proceed. Decision owners: lead (Ava) + Marcus + Liam.
- Final demo + 30-minute review with Eng Leadership and Product at end of Week 6.

Risks and mitigations
- Risk: Instrumentation causes unexpected latency. Mitigation: Benchmark SDK changes in a canary cluster, keep sampling low, and rollback easily.
- Risk: Alerts spam during tuning. Mitigation: Start with conservative thresholds and a "mute window" for the first tuning pass.
- Risk: Ownership confusion between teams. Mitigation: clear owner matrix (below) and a short runbook mapping which team owns which signal.

Owner matrix (quick reference)
- Metric instrumentation and SDK changes: serving-runtime (Marcus)
- Metrics ingestion, retention, and dashboards: observability (Liam)
- Alerting policies & incident flows: eng-sre (Ava)
- Product adoption vetting, onboarding docs: product-hosted-api (Priya)
- Developer-facing demo and workshop: solutions-engineering (Sofia)

Deliverables
- Working Grafana dashboard and alerting policy for pilot route.
- Short adoption checklist and SLO template (one-liner SLI definitions, alert thresholds, escalation matrix).
- Post-prototype report: experiments, blind spots, cost estimate, recommended rollout sequence for next 3 services.

Next steps (immediate)
1) Kickoff invite: schedule 2-hour kickoff this week.
2) Provision load generator and ephemeral cluster by Marcus.
3) Create tickets: SRE-789 (instrumentation), RELPROJ-12 (dashboard + alerts).

Notes to self / working questions
- Are we comfortable with 7d retention for prototype metrics? If not, note cost tradeoffs for 30d.
- Do we need a separate PD escalation policy for model-fallback incidents vs hardware failures?

Raw links and references
- Confluence experiment notebook (working): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/ops-slo-lab-notes
- Existing SLO templates (read-only): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/SLO-templates

-- end of prototype charter --
